hints: Focus on what it means for X2+ to be isoelectronic with krypton, think about how many electrons each particle actually has.
Krypton is $Z = 36$ with configuration $[Ar]4s^23d^{10}4p^6$, so X2+ has 36 electrons which means neutral X must have 38 electrons.
Remember that 2+ ions of s-block metals are formed by removing the outermost $s$ electrons first, so to go back to the atom just add those two electrons into the next $s$ subshell.
walkthrough:
**Find the electrons in X2+**

The ion X2+ has the same configuration as Kr. Kr has atomic number 36, so it has 36 electrons.

Kr configuration:
$$[Ar]4s^2 3d^{10} 4p^6$$

**Work back to the neutral atom X**

X2+ was made by removing 2 electrons from X. So X must have 2 more electrons than X2+.
$$36 + 2 = 38 \text{ electrons in atom X}$$

**Add the electrons to the correct subshell**

For Period 5 s-block metals, the 2 electrons are lost from the $5s$ subshell when the ion forms. To rebuild the atom, we add them back to $5s$.
$$[Ar]4s^2 3d^{10} 4p^6 + 5s^2 = [Ar]4s^2 3d^{10} 4p^6 5s^2$$
This is strontium, $Z = 38$, and matches the correct choice.

options.A: This is exactly the configuration of Kr and of X2+, with 36 electrons. It forgets to add back the 2 electrons removed to form the 2+ ion, so it describes the ion, not the neutral atom X.
options.B: This adds $5s^2$ to the Kr core, giving 38 electrons total. This is correct because neutral X has two more electrons than X2+, and those fill the outermost 5s subshell.
options.C: This still has only 36 electrons, so it cannot be neutral X. It also incorrectly writes $4d^{10}$ instead of $3d^{10}$. Remember the 3d subshell fills after 4s, not 4d.
options.D: This has the right number of electrons (38) but labels the d subshell wrongly as $4d^{10}$ instead of $3d^{10}$. The d subshell in the Kr core is 3d, and that does not change when you add $5s^2$.
